newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf Arabs call on Turkey to withdraw from Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Arabs call on Turkey to withdraw from Iraq.

text.p: Gulf Arab foreign ministers on Saturday said Turkey's incursion into northern Iraq posed a threat to international peace.

"Based on our firm stance with regards to the necessity of preserving Iraq's independence and sovereignty, we call on Turkey to withdraw its troops from Iraqi territory," Qatar's Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani said.
Sheikh Hamad was speaking at the opening session of a two-day meeting of Gulf Cooperation Council foreign ministers in Riyadh.
He said Turkish military operations inside Iraq constituted a violation of Iraq's territorial integrity.

Thousands of Turkish troops, backed by air power, poured into northern Iraq on May 14 in pursuit of separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels who they say use the region as a base to launch raids into southeast Turkey.
The troops are in the Iraqi Kurdish enclave that was once set up as a "safe haven" by Western allies after the Gulf War when rebellious Kurds were pursued by Baghdad troops.
Ministers from Saudi Arabia, Kuwait Oman, Qatar the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain had been scheduled to meet in Riyadh on June 7. It was not clear why the talks were brought forward.
